title: Vega OS: Screen and controls
lead: Use the Vega OS TV screen with a remote to check sources, playback settings, subtitles, API results and events.

blocks.text: Scroll the controls and editors below the video. Source and Playback contain the main controls. Use D-pad and Select on a device, or arrow keys and Enter on a Vega Virtual Device. The outline marks current focus; greyed controls are unavailable or already selected. There is no browser Player control bar or HTML theme picker.

blocks.title: Display language
blocks.text: Use the language selector to switch between English and Japanese. Screenshots on this page use English; SDK names, code and returned data keep their original spelling. Select the content’s subtitle language separately.

blocks.title: Before opening the screen
blocks.text: Use the Kepler build for Vega OS; an Android-based Fire TV package cannot run here. The app ID is com.playerlab.vega and the component is com.playerlab.vega.main. After a license change, regenerate local runtime configuration and rebuild. Follow the startup instructions below for the SDK setup and target-device selection.

items.label: Build and launch the Kepler app
Integrate the Kepler host and Player

blocks.text: Choose a source and apply a change

blocks.caption: The configuration form below the native video shows the source URL, type, title, poster and external subtitle fields. More settings continue below this capture.

items: Select a VOD preset and check that the picture and position advance. Autoplay and startup mute are initially on. If autoplay is off, run PlayerAPI.play in SDK API experiments.

Open Show configuration and record the values to restore. Enter an HTTP/HTTPS URL and match HLS, DASH or progressive MP4 to the media. Title and poster are stored, but this screen does not render a poster image.
Keep the URL unchanged, enter a 5-second start offset, select Start, then Apply and recreate player. Compare position and the picture after loading.
Even a source-only change recreates the Player and reloads from the configured offset. Invalid values or an unchanged configuration leave the current session in place.

Reset draft discards pending edits only. To undo an applied change, enter the original values and Apply. To restore Player defaults, turn autoplay and startup mute on, and clear both buffer fields and maximum video bitrate. A VOD preset restores source fields only.

rows: Compare the position after Apply. Start refers to the media or live-window beginning; End refers to its end or the live edge. Signed offsets are supported.
Compare the new session after Apply. Use PlayerAPI.play when autoplay is off. These switches do not directly pause or unmute the current session.
Use positive values for the forward-buffer targets; clear them for SDK defaults. They do not extend the live rewind window.
Enter the number without units or commas, then compare selected quality and playback on a multi-quality source. Clear it to remove the cap.

blocks.text: Enter a finite decimal start offset in seconds and positive buffer and bitrate values. The implementation guide lists SDK defaults, configuration paths and the supported Vega transport.

items.label: Configuration meanings, units, defaults and Fetch transport

blocks.caption: A plain WebVTT cue displayed over the native video. The settings below it remain usable; this is an app-rendered text overlay rather than the browser subtitle UI.

items: Enable autoplay or use PlayerAPI.play and PlayerAPI.pause in SDK API experiments. On live content with a rewind window, compare Live edge, rewind buttons, position and status. Allow DVR toggles the app’s helper.
Enter an HTTPS WebVTT URL reachable from the device, a label and a language tag such as en-US. Match subtitle cue times to the media.
Turn on Enable external subtitle on load, Apply, then play through a cue. This switch enables the track; no browser subtitle-menu selection is needed.
To remove the track, clear its URL and Apply. Its label and language are also cleared. Reset draft does not remove an applied subtitle. Rendering uses plain text, without HTML styling.

blocks.title: Returning to the app
blocks.text: Returning from the background creates a new session from the retained source and applied settings, using its start offset and Autoplay choice. It does not restore an arbitrary previous position. If the app reports that native media release is unconfirmed, restart the app before trying again; repeated Apply cannot confirm that the old media resources were released.

blocks.caption: Show applied code in the Vega app. Code lines can receive remote focus so the ScrollView reveals lines below the video. License values use placeholders.

items: After Apply, open Show applied code. Compare source and Player settings with your previous record. The output contains applied values and allowed function bodies, excluding pending edits. Licenses and sensitive headers use placeholders.
Move focus up or down through the lines to scroll the output. This TV app has no clipboard-copy integration.
Opening the output after an unapplied edit leaves it unchanged. Reset draft discards that edit; restoring applied values requires entering the original values and applying.
See the implementation guide for the native-media connection. Copying these settings into a browser does not reproduce this host’s playback environment.

blocks.caption: The typed configuration editor shows a callback signature, body and explicit permission control. Apply installs the approved callback before the matching request is tried.

items: Open Show configuration → Show all SDK configuration. Search for a PlayerConfig or SourceConfig path and choose Set Vega API value.

Follow the displayed type for numbers, strings, enums, objects, maps, arrays or bytes. Add array items in order and complete required fields. Record current values and whether an override was already enabled.

For a function, enter its JavaScript body, check the argument and return contract, then enable Allow this callback. Try the matching operation after Apply. Value factories and SDK callbacks run at different times; check the implementation guide’s conditions.

Compare applied code with results and events. Removing an override and applying restores the basic form or SDK default. A removed callback is no longer called after replacement. Also restore Player state changed by its body.

blocks.text: JavaScript runs inside the app without a sandbox; allow only trusted code. Binary inputs accept hexadecimal or Base64. See the implementation guide for type conversion and native-feature constraints.

items.label: Typed inputs, callbacks and configuration application

blocks.text: Run commands and inspect state and events

Search by an API path, method name or a feature such as volume or subtitles. English and Japanese search terms work, and exact paths and method names appear first. Previous results and Next results move through all matches; changing the search returns to the first result page.

blocks.caption: PlayerAPI.getCurrentTime during playback. The result appears below Run Vega SDK API; the picture and SDK events provide additional context.

items: Open Show SDK API experiments, search PlayerAPI.getCurrentTime and choose a call signature if needed. Optional arguments can be supplied or omitted. Select Run Vega SDK API. Executed call displays the submitted code; Result displays the returned value, while API error identifies a failed call or input validation.

Run the time query again while media advances, and compare seconds with the picture. Inspect current SDK API availability only checks whether methods exist; it does not call them or demonstrate their feature behavior.

To compare a command, read PlayerAPI.getVolume, record its value, run PlayerAPI.setVolume and read it again. Restore the recorded volume afterward. A returned value, a setter or an empty result should be checked against the relevant state/events.

Use SDK events, Pause Vega event log and Clear Vega event log to isolate the relevant notifications. For on/off experiments, remove the same callback instance that was registered. Query any required SDK objects from the current session after recreation.

Use Recreate Vega player after destroying the Player or to return to the applied configuration. The replacement waits for the previous media session to release. It does not undo saved source/configuration changes; restore those in the form when needed.

blocks.caption: The SDK returned volume 17 after a callback changed it in this captured experiment. Compare a setter with the getter, then restore the value recorded before your own test.

blocks.text: Try HLS, DASH and live-specific APIs with matching formats and content. Method availability and working behavior on a Vega device are separate checks. See the implementation guide for format, low-latency and native-feature prerequisites.

items: Use an HLS source containing insertion markers; the Vega README links a public sample. In Show all SDK configuration, select PlayerConfig.tweaks.enable_sgai_handling, choose true and Apply.
In SDK API experiments, inspect PlayerAPI.sgai.list for the schedule. PlayerAPI.sgai.getActiveAd reports the active inserted content and is normally empty outside an insertion interval.

While an applicable insertion is active, try PlayerAPI.sgai.skip and compare AdStarted, AdSkipped, AdBreakFinished and subsequent playback. A scheduled insertion alone does not show that the content was reached.
To end the experiment, restore the previous source and remove the SGAI override if it was added, then Apply. Compare the loaded source and applied code with the recorded baseline.

blocks.text: If a scheduled position falls outside the media range, check the stream and interstitial timestamps. The implementation guide describes SGAI configuration, events and platform prerequisites.
